subjective.citation_text: Patient: I'm 35, male. I've been having some back pain again, especially on the left side. It's been bothering me for a while now, and I wanted to check in. Doctor: Could you please provide your age, gender, and describe the nature, duration, and any associated symptoms of your back pain? Patient: I'm 35, male. I've been having some back pain again, especially on the left side. It's been bothering me for a while now, and I wanted to check in. The pain is pretty random, sometimes it just happens, and it's worse when I bend over. My significant other says stretching helps, which it usually does. Doctor: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your legs or feet associated with the back pain? Stretching usually helps, though. Doctor: Have you experienced any prior injuries or conditions related to your back, such as previous fractures, herniated discs, or surgeries? Patient: Yes, I had back surgery in November of 2020. It was a microdiscectomy because my disk broke off and wrapped around my spinal thecal sac. It was a pretty horrible experience, but at least it wasn't the poop sac. I had a lot of nerve pain down my leg and in my back, and I was on a high dose of gabapentin for it. It was tough to get off of. Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies, such as an MRI or X-ray, since your 2020 microdiscectomy? If so, could you provide the dates and results of these examinations? Patient: I don't have any imaging studies done since my surgery, but when I came in today, they took an X-ray and it showed that there are no fractures or issues with the spinal bone.
